facts.statement: Eomamenchisaurus is a mamenchisaurid sauropod dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic of Yuanmou, Yunnan, China.
facts.quote: Eomamenchisaurus (meaning "dawn Mamenchisaurus") is a genus of mamenchisaurid sauropod dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic Zhanghe Formation of Yuanmou, Yunnan, China.

facts.statement: The type species E. yuanmouensis was described by Lü Junchang and colleagues in 2008.
facts.quote: The type species is E. yuanmouensis, described by Lü Junchang and colleagues in 2008.

facts.statement: The animal is known only from a single partial skeleton (holotype CXMVZA 165) containing vertebrae, pelvic bones, and leg bones.
facts.quote: Eomamenchisaurus yuanmouensis is only known from a single partial skeleton, the holotype CXMVZA 165, which includes incomplete cervical vertebrae, dorsal vertebrae, a partial sacrum consisting of three preserved vertebrae, the right ilium, pubis, and tibia, and both femora and ischia.

facts.statement: Eomamenchisaurus belonged to the mamenchisaurid group, which is typically characterized by a very long neck.
facts.quote: Eomamenchisaurus was a mamenchisaurid, a group of sauropods typically characterized by a very long neck.

facts.statement: In several respects, Eomamenchisaurus displays more primitive characteristics than other mamenchisaurids.
facts.quote: However, in several respects, Eomamenchisaurus shows more primitive characteristics than other mamenchisaurids.

facts.statement: The femur of Eomamenchisaurus is 1.1 meters long, similar to the femur of the 16-meter-long Mamenchisaurus youngi.
facts.quote: The femur is 1.1 m long, similar in length to the 1.16 m long femur of the 16 m long Mamenchisaurus youngi.

facts.statement: Lü and colleagues originally classified Eomamenchisaurus as a mamenchisaurid.
facts.quote: Lü and colleagues, in their original description of Eomamenchisaurus, classified it as a mamenchisaurid.

facts.statement: In 2015, researchers noted that Eomamenchisaurus was difficult to distinguish from the related genus Yuanmousaurus.
facts.quote: In 2015, Xing Lida and colleagues noted that Eomamenchisaurus was difficult to distinguish from Yuanmousaurus, another mamenchisaurid from the Zhanghe Formation.

facts.statement: Eomamenchisaurus lived between 174.7 and 161.5 million years ago during the Aalenian to Callovian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Aalenian to Callovian (174.7 to 161.5 million years ago)

rejected.quote: Eomamenchisaurus yuanmouensis was named by Lü Junchang, Li Tianguang, Zhong Shimin, Ji Qiang, and Li Shaoxue in 2008 based on a partial skeleton found in Jiangyi Township of Yuanmou County, Yunnan.
